Directory raptor/code/
The `raptor/code/` directory is responsible for codebase indexing, hybrid search, graph building, and Q&A over repositories. 

Main components include:
- `CodeIndex` (`index.py`), the central class managing index building, saving, loading, and querying.
- `CodeTreeBuilder` (`build.py`) and `CodeGraphBuilder` (`graph.py`), which construct hierarchical code DAGs and static code graphs.
- `CodeSearcher` (`search.py`) and `BM25` (`lexical.py`), providing hybrid retrieval using RRF and lexical search.
- `PythonExtractor` (`languages/python.py`) and `make_extractors` (`languages/__init__.py`), handling per-language syntactic analysis.
- `CodeConfig` (`config.py`), `CodeModelsConfig` (`models.py`), and `CodeSearcher` handle configuration and model execution.
- `code_app` (`cli.py`) and `create_server` (`mcp_server.py`), exposing CLI commands and MCP server workflows.

Public entry points are exported via `raptor.code.__init__.py`, including `CodeIndex`, `CodeConfig`, `CodeAnswer`, `CodeEdge`, and `CodeHit`. It depends on internal `raptor` modules and external libraries like `tree_sitter`, `tiktoken`, and `typer`.

Directory raptor/
The `raptor/` directory implements Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval, managing hierarchical text chunking, embedding, clustering, indexing, retrieval, and code repository analysis. 

Main components include `raptor/__init__.py` and ⁠`raptor/pipeline.py` providing high-level entry points like `RetrievalAugmentation`, ⁠`raptor/builder.py` (`TreeBuilder`) for hierarchical tree construction, ⁠`raptor/types.py` (`Tree`, `Node`), and `raptor/storage.py` (`save_tree`, `load_tree`). Repository raptor
Raptor implements recursive abstractive processing for tree-organized document retrieval. It splits text into chunks, clusters them, and recursively summarizes clusters to build a hierarchical index. 

Public entry points include the Python classes `RetrievalAugmentation`, `TreeBuilder`, `TreeRetriever`, `Chunker`, and the `raptor` CLI tool (`build`, `ask`, `info`). Requests flow through `RetrievalAugmentation` and `TreeBuilder` (in `raptor/pipeline.py` and `raptor/builder.py`), which orchestrate text chunking (`raptor/chunking`), clustering (`raptor/clustering`), and tree indexing (`raptor/storage.py`), before retrieving nodes via `TreeRetriever` (`raptor/retrieval`) to answer questions. 

Key external dependencies include NumPy, Pydantic, scikit-learn, and integrations for Gemini, Ollama, and sentence-transformers.

Concept: Question-Answering Model Abstraction and Caching
Concept: Question-Answering Model Abstraction and Caching

These files implement a pluggable question-answering architecture using the `BaseQAModel` abstract base class in `raptor/models/base.py`, which defines `answer_question` and `stream_answer`. 

The `CachedQAModel` in `raptor/models/cache.py` acts as a decorator wrapper implementing the same interface while adding disk caching and proxying extra methods via `__getattr__`. 

Concrete implementations include `FakeQAModel` in `raptor/server/fakes.py`, which performs sentence-overlap extraction for testing, and `KeywordQA` in `tests/test_eval.py`, a JSON-mode reader used in evaluations. 

A developer should look at `raptor/models/base.py` first to understand the core QA interface, followed by `raptor/models/cache.py` to see how caching is layered on top.

Concept: Model Lifecycle and Management
Concept: Model Lifecycle and Management

These files manage AI model instantiation, caching, and dependency injection across the application. 

`raptor/models/__init__.py` acts as the core factory, using `build_models` to instantiate embedding, summarization, and QA models into a `ModelBundle`, optionally wrapping them with disk caching via `with_cache`. 

`raptor/server/fakes.py` provides deterministic offline alternatives (`FakeEmbeddingModel`, `FakeSummarizationModel`, `FakeQAModel`, and `fake_bundle`) for testing and demos without network dependencies. 

`raptor/server/app.py::_Models` bridges these components by lazily providing either real models or injected/fake models (`ModelBundle`) to server requests. It determines whether to operate offline and configures models per build using settings and configuration.

A developer should look at `raptor/models/__init__.py` first to understand real model initialization, and `raptor/server/app.py::_Models` to see how models are supplied to the server runtime.

Concept: Rate Limiting
Concept: Rate Limiting

These components work together to provide thread-safe, sliding-window rate limiting. The core logic resides in `raptor/models/ratelimit.py`, driven by the `RateLimiter` class. `RateLimiter.__init__` initializes a thread lock and a timestamp deque based on an optional requests-per-minute (`rpm`) limit. 

When a caller interacts with `RateLimiter`, `try_acquire(cost)` evaluates if slots are available within a 60-second window, mutating internal state and returning `0.0` on success or the required wait time in seconds. If blocking is needed, `acquire()` calls `time.sleep` until `try_acquire` succeeds. Additionally, `shared_limiter(name, rpm)` manages process-wide named limiter buckets. 

A developer should look at `raptor/models/ratelimit.py` first, specifically the `RateLimiter` class and its `try_acquire` method.

Concept: Multiple-choice question answering and caching evaluation

The `raptor.eval.answering` module implements QuALITY dataset multiple-choice question answering using reader models with disk caching. 

Developers should look at `MCQAnswerer` in `raptor/eval/answering.py` first. This class orchestrates the answering process via its `answer(context, question, options)` method, backed by disk caching. It can be instantiated directly or through `from_qa_model()`, which selects between JSON mode and plain text with regex. 

Helper functions support this workflow: `format_prompt()` prepares inputs into `MCQ_PROMPT`, while `parse_answer()` extracts the final option and rationale from the model's raw output. The process yields an `MCQAnswer` dataclass containing the result and metadata, utilizing `DiskCache` for persistence and thread locking for safety.

Concept: persistence and caching layer
Concept: persistence and caching layer

These files implement caching for model calls and tree projections to ensure deterministic and cost-free re-runs. 

`raptor/models/cache.py` provides `DiskCache`, a thread-safe SQLite key-value store, and management helpers like `open_cache` alongside model wrappers (`CachedEmbeddingModel`, `CachedSummarizationModel`, `CachedQAModel`). It handles raw byte-level I/O and tracks performance through `CacheStats`. 

`raptor/server/projection.py` uses local disk storage to cache two-dimensional tree node projections. The `project` function computes UMAP or PCA coordinates from a `Tree`, while `cached_projection` handles reading and writing these results as JSON files under a specified directory using a thread lock.

A developer should look at `raptor/models/cache.py` first to understand core data storage, and then `raptor/server/projection.py` for feature-specific JSON caching.

Concept: API key rate-limiting and failover management
Concept: API key rate-limiting and failover management

The `raptor.models.keypool` module manages multiple Gemini API keys with rate-limiting, error handling, and failover. A developer should look at `KeyPool` in `raptor/models/keypool.py` first. `KeyPool` uses `KeySlot` to track client instances and integrates with `RateLimiter` to control request rates per bucket. It provides `acquire()` to find an available key and `call()` to execute functions with automatic failover and retries. Error helpers like `is_rate_limit()` and `is_auth_error()` determine failure types, while `QuotaExhaustedError` signals depleted daily quotas. `shared_pool()` supplies a process-wide singleton. `tests/test_keypool.py` validates these behaviors using mocked errors and settings.

Concept: Hybrid and Lexical Retrieval
Concept: Hybrid and Lexical Retrieval

These files and classes implement lexical search and passage reranking. A developer should look first at `raptor/code/lexical.py`, which provides the text preprocessing functions (`split_identifier`, `tokenize`) and the code-specific `BM25` class for sparse postings and scoring (`scores`, `top`). For general text search, `raptor/retrieval/hybrid.py` provides another dependency-free `BM25` class that operates over a fixed list of raw string documents and returns an array of scores. Finally, `raptor/models/local.py` provides the `CrossEncoderReranker` class, which uses a local cross-encoder model to score and rerank (query, passage) pairs via its `score` method for higher relevance precision.

Concept: Retrieval and ranking layer
Concept: Retrieval and ranking layer

These files implement the retrieval and ranking mechanisms for RAPTOR. A developer should start at `raptor/retrieval/base.py`, which defines `RetrievalResult` and `RetrievedNode` to manage retrieved nodes and format context, while `score_all` computes vector similarities against a tree. For advanced post-processing, `raptor/retrieval/hybrid.py` provides ranking and fusion utilities. It includes `BM25` for lexical scoring, `rrf` for Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and `mmr` for Maximal Marginal Relevance reordering. Additionally, `hybrid.py` supplies `get_reranker` to manage cached cross-encoder instances via the `Reranker` protocol, integrating dense and sparse retrieval strategies.

Concept: retrieval and search execution
Concept: retrieval and search execution

These pieces work together to perform document retrieval and question answering over text indices using hierarchical RAPTOR trees and flat baselines. A developer should look at `raptor/server/indexes.py::Searcher` first, as it acts as a facade uniting the components. `Searcher` delegates hierarchical queries to `TreeRetriever` in `raptor/retrieval/tree_retriever.py`, which executes search strategies like `collapsed` ranking or top-down `traversal` across tree nodes. For baseline comparisons, `Searcher` utilizes `FlatRAG` from `raptor/retrieval/flat.py`, which performs dense retrieval exclusively over leaf chunks using cosine similarity. Together, `TreeRetriever`, `FlatRAG`, and `Searcher` handle scoring, filtering, token budgeting, and answer generation.

Concept: RAPTOR Pipeline API and Configuration
Concept: RAPTOR Pipeline API and Configuration

`raptor/pipeline.py` provides a high-level API for managing RAPTOR indices. Developers should look at `RetrievalAugmentation` in `raptor/pipeline.py` first, as it is the primary class coordinating the entire workflow. 

`RetrievalAugmentation` initializes models, builds trees via `_builder()`, retrieves nodes via `retriever()`, answers questions using `answer_question()`, and persists data with `save()`. It handles operations like `add_documents()` and `add_to_existing()` to process text inputs into `Tree` objects. 

`RetrievalAugmentationConfig` supports backward compatibility by mapping legacy keyword arguments and model instances onto `RaptorConfig`. The module relies on supporting components like `.builder`, `.retrieval`, `.models`, and `.storage` to execute tree construction, retrieval, and disk I/O.

Concept: Hybrid code retrieval and search caching
Concept: Hybrid code retrieval and search caching

`CodeSearcher` in `raptor/code/search.py` performs hybrid code retrieval by combining BM25, dense scores, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, query routing, tree descent, and graph expansion. It accepts queries and configuration options in its `search` method to return ranked `CodeHit` objects, while `neighbors` tracks callers, callees, and inheritance. 

`SearcherCache` in `raptor/server/indexes.py` manages lifecycle caching by holding one searcher instance per index identifier, modification time, and embedding model via its `get` method. 

A developer should look at `raptor/code/search.py` and `CodeSearcher` first to understand the retrieval logic, query types, and scoring mechanisms.

Concept: background job management and event streaming
Concept: background job management and event streaming

`raptor/server/jobs.py` coordinates background task execution and client event streaming. `JobManager` runs submitted tasks sequentially using a `ThreadPoolExecutor` and stores `Job` instances in memory. It provides methods like `submit()`, `get()`, and `shutdown()`. Each `Job` tracks execution status, results, and logs timed events via `emit()`. It also exposes a `stream()` method to replay events and follow live updates. Concurrently, `raptor/server/builds.py::_Tracker` maintains shared state specifically for build wrappers, such as node texts and cluster-to-parent mappings.

A developer should look first at `JobManager` in `raptor/server/jobs.py` to understand how jobs are queued and executed, then examine `Job` for event emission and SSE streaming.

Concept: Evaluation Runner and Tree Storage

These classes manage the execution of RAPTOR evaluation experiments and article tree caching. 

Developers should look at `Runner` in `raptor/eval/runner.py` first, which coordinates evaluations. `Runner.__init__` sets up directories, models, and workers. `Runner.run` and `Runner.run_file` execute individual experiments, producing `RunOutcome` results, while `Runner.run_many` handles multiple paths. 

`Runner` delegates tree management to `TreeStore`, which persists and retrieves tree structures on disk. `TreeStore.get_or_build` checks or generates trees keyed by article and configuration via `TreeStore.key` and `TreeStore.path`. `Runner` also accesses helper methods like `Runner.articles`, `Runner.answerer`, and `Runner.cache`.

These classes implement hierarchical token-limited text clustering for embeddings. `TokenLimitedClustering` acts as the base class, managing token limits and validation via `cluster` and `_limited`. It delegates the actual grouping logic to subclasses through the `groups` method. `KMeansSilhouetteClustering` inherits from `TokenLimitedClustering` and implements this specific `groups` method by performing k-means clustering on unit vectors, automatically selecting the optimal cluster count `k` using the cosine silhouette score while ensuring the smallest `k` respects the token limit.

A developer should look first at `TokenLimitedClustering.cluster` in `raptor/clustering/strategies.py` to understand the entry point for validation and token-budget enforcement, then inspect `KMeansSilhouetteClustering.groups` for the silhouette-based k-selection algorithm.

Concept: Embedding Clustering Strategies
Concept: Embedding Clustering Strategies

These classes implement different clustering algorithms for text embeddings within a token-limited framework. They all inherit from `TokenLimitedClustering` and implement a `groups` method to organize embeddings (`np.ndarray`) and tokens (`np.ndarray`) into grouped indices (`list[list[int]]`). 

`GMMClustering` applies a soft Gaussian Mixture Model directly to embeddings without reduction. `PCAGMMClustering` first reduces dimensions using PCA before applying soft GMM. `HDBSCANClustering` reduces dimensions via UMAP and applies sklearn's HDBSCAN, reassigning noise points to the nearest cluster. 

A developer should look at `raptor/clustering/strategies.py` first to inspect these implementations and select or modify a strategy's initialization parameters and grouping logic.

Concept: document tree clustering strategies
Concept: document tree clustering strategies

These classes work together to provide alternative algorithms for grouping text nodes within the RAPTOR retrieval architecture, inheriting token-limited constraints to build hierarchical text summaries. 

A developer should look at `raptor/clustering/strategies.py` first. Inside this module, `AgglomerativeClustering` implements average-linkage hierarchical clustering using cosine distance via its `groups` method, supporting a `distance_threshold` or `target_size` to limit cluster growth. Alternatively, `ContiguousClustering` segments ordered nodes into adjacent runs using dynamic programming in its `_best_cuts` helper and main `groups` method, minimizing cut-point similarity to maintain narrative sequence across tree layers. Both classes implement the `TokenLimitedClustering` interface to produce index lists (`list[list[int]]`) representing grouped text embeddings and tokens.

Concept: hierarchical tree construction
Concept: hierarchical tree construction

These components build hierarchical RAPTOR trees from text and codebases. Developers should look at `TreeBuilder` in `raptor/builder.py` and `CodeTreeBuilder` in `raptor/code/build.py` first.

`TreeBuilder` constructs general text trees by repeatedly chunking, embedding, clustering, and summarizing via `build_from_text` and `build_from_chunks`. It relies on models (`BaseEmbeddingModel`, `BaseSummarizationModel`) and configuration (`RaptorConfig`).

`CodeTreeBuilder` specializes in software repositories. Its `build` method orchestrates hierarchical DAG construction from symbol leaves through classes, files, directories, repository nodes, and concepts using methods like `_build_classes`, `_build_files`, and `_build_concepts`. It utilizes `Reuse` and `BuildStats` to optimize incremental builds by caching and hashing unchanged embeddings and summaries. Both builders output a `Tree` object.

Concept: Code repository indexing and retrieval
Concept: Code repository indexing and retrieval

These components implement code repository parsing, embedding, and search capabilities. The core engine is `CodeIndex` in `raptor/code/index.py`, which parses repositories, builds graph structures, computes embeddings, and handles persistence via `save` and `load`. Finally, `CodeService` in `raptor/server/code.py` manages multiple code repositories and exposes these indexing operations to the server interface. 

Developers should look at `CodeIndex` in `raptor/code/index.py` first to understand core indexing and search logic.

Concept: RAPTOR index and search data structures
Concept: RAPTOR index and search data structures

These files and modules define the core structural and result types for the RAPTOR index. Start by looking at `raptor/types.py`, which implements the foundational index graph via the `Node` and `Tree` classes. `Node` represents a single leaf chunk or summary with text, index, children, and embeddings, while `Tree` manages the full layered DAG, offering querying helpers like `parents_of`, `nodes_in_layer`, `normalized_matrix`, and structural validation via `validate()`. 

Complementing this, `raptor/code/types.py` provides data structures for code-specific search results and graph relationships. It defines `CodeHit` for retrieved nodes with citation formatting, `CodeAnswer` to bundle answers with hits, and the `CodeEdge` dataclass for graph connections.

Concept: text chunking strategies

These files and classes implement text segmentation strategies to split documents into `Chunk` objects. A developer should start by looking at `raptor/chunking/sentence.py`, which provides the base `SentenceChunker` class and sentence-greedy parsing logic via `_units`, `_token_windows`, and `_clause_spans`. 

`raptor/chunking/strategies.py` builds upon this foundation with two concrete strategies. `FixedTokenChunker` creates uniform sliding-window segments defined by `max_tokens` and `overlap_tokens`. `SemanticChunker` inherits from `SentenceChunker` and splits text based on embedding similarity drops using an `embedding_model`, ignoring overlap tokens. It uses `_merge_small` and `_pack` to adjust segments around a `breakpoint_percentile` threshold and `min_tokens` constraints.

That module defines `_Ollama`, a base helper class managing HTTP communication via its `_post` and `_generate` methods, and `OllamaSummarizationModel`, which inherits from `_Ollama` and `BaseSummarizationModel` to implement the `summarize` method with configurable parameters like `model_name`, `host`, and `timeout`. Concept: embedding model architecture and wrappers
Concept: embedding model architecture and wrappers

These files implement text vectorization using an abstract base class and various wrapper and concrete implementations. Developers should look at `raptor/models/base.py::BaseEmbeddingModel` first, which defines the core interface via `embed_documents` and `embed_query`. 

Concrete implementations include `SBertEmbeddingModel` in `raptor/models/local.py` for Sentence-Transformers, `FakeEmbeddingModel` in `raptor/server/fakes.py` using feature hashing, and `FixedQuery` in `tests/test_retrieval.py` for testing.

Concept: Model Management and Abstraction Layer
Concept: Model Management and Abstraction Layer

These files work together to define, instantiate, and manage AI models for embeddings, summarization, and question answering. 

`raptor/models/base.py` is the starting point for developers. It defines the abstract interfaces (`BaseEmbeddingModel`, `BaseSummarizationModel`, `BaseQAModel`) that all providers must implement. 

`raptor/models/local.py` provides concrete local implementations, specifically `SBertEmbeddingModel` (using `sentence_transformers`) and `CrossEncoderReranker`, returning numpy arrays.

`raptor/code/models.py` handles code-specific model wiring. It exposes builder functions and `LazyModels`, which delays instantiation until first use—avoiding unnecessary API key checks for read-only commands—and handles caching and network-backed model calls.

Concept: Google Gemini model integration

`GeminiEmbeddingModel` inherits `BaseEmbeddingModel` and implements `_embed`, `_embed_batch`, `embed_documents`, and `embed_query` to convert text sequences into NumPy arrays.

Developers should look at `raptor/models/gemini.py` first to inspect API configurations, rate limits, or model wrappers.

Concept: Summarization model decorators and implementations

Concept: testing infrastructure and offline mock models
Concept: testing infrastructure and offline mock models

The `tests/conftest.py` module provides shared Pytest fixtures and mock implementations for deterministic offline testing. A developer should look here first when investigating test setup or missing mock behaviors. 

It defines three mock models inheriting from base classes: `HashEmbedder`, `EchoSummarizer`, and `EchoQA`. `HashEmbedder` implements text-to-vector conversion using hashed bag-of-words via its `vector()` and `embed_documents()` methods. `EchoSummarizer` and `EchoQA` handle text summarization and question answering through `summarize()` and `answer_question()`. Additionally, `make_document()` generates synthetic multi-topic text. 

The module wires these into reusable Pytest fixtures (`embedder`, `summarizer`, `qa`, and `document`), mutating only in-memory call counters during test execution.

Concept: experiment evaluation harness
Concept: experiment evaluation harness

These files implement an evaluation harness for running, analyzing, and reporting on experiments. A developer should look at `raptor/eval/runner.py` first, as its `Runner` class and `ExperimentConfig` orchestrate executing YAML-configured QuALITY experiments, building trees via `TreeStore`, and managing disk caching. Finished artifacts are queried and compared via `raptor/eval/runs.py`, which provides functions like `list_runs`, `load_run`, and `compare_runs`. The module `raptor/eval/report.py` then consumes these run artifacts using `stage_rows` and `generate_report` to write Markdown summaries and matplotlib figures. Finally, `tests/test_eval.py` exercises the entire workflow—including `KeywordQA`, model caching, metrics, and resumption—using local file I/O.

Concept: QuALITY evaluation and retrieval comparison
Concept: QuALITY evaluation and retrieval comparison

These files work together to load, serve, and evaluate the QuALITY dataset for RAPTOR retrieval comparisons. 

Developers should look first at `raptor/eval/datasets/quality.py`, which defines the foundational data structures (`QualityQuestion`, `QualityArticle`) and data-loading functions (`load_quality`, `iter_quality`) using standard library disk I/O. 

Next, `raptor/server/quality.py` consumes these structures via the `QualityStore` class, adding thread-safe access, serialization helpers (`story_summary`, `question_dict`), and lookup methods to support a UI library picker and arena. 

Finally, `examples/quality_compare.py` uses `load_quality` alongside `RetrievalAugmentation`, `FlatRAG`, and Gemini models configured via `models_for` to execute command-line retrieval evaluations and parse predicted options via `predicted_option`.

Concept: QuALITY Dataset Management and Artifact Generation
Concept: QuALITY Dataset Management and Artifact Generation

These scripts work together to download, analyze, and generate synthetic artifacts for the QuALITY dataset. 

A developer should look at `scripts/download_quality.py` first, which uses `main()` to fetch or copy dataset splits into `data/quality`. Next, `scripts/dataset_plots.py` procedurally reads these splits to generate exploratory data analysis figures in `docs/figures/`. 

For testing and evaluation, `scripts/make_fixture_runs.py` loads the dataset using `load_quality` and creates synthetic test fixtures in `tests/fixtures/runs/` using helper functions like `fingerprint` and `wilson`. Finally, `scripts/synth_runs.py` synthesizes complete experiment run artifacts, configs, and summaries using functions like `synth_results`, `synth_summary`, and `write_run` based on baseline data.

Concept: evaluation and experimentation framework
Concept: evaluation and experimentation framework

These files implement the QuALITY evaluation and experimentation framework for Raptor. 

`raptor/eval/__init__.py` marks the evaluation module boundary. `raptor/eval/cli.py` serves as the primary entry point, providing a Typer command-line interface (`app`) that orchestrates experiment execution, run management, comparisons, reporting, and dataset splitting by calling internal modules. `raptor/eval/splits.py` handles the creation, serialization via YAML, and loading of fixed, seeded dataset splits using `SplitSpec` and `QualityArticle`. Finally, `raptor/eval/metrics.py` computes statistical evaluation metrics—such as accuracy, bootstrap confidence intervals, McNemar tests, and tree statistics—purely in memory without side effects.

A developer should look at `raptor/eval/cli.py` first to understand user-facing commands and workflow integration.

Concept: server setup and api contract
Concept: server setup and api contract

These files work together to provide the backend foundation for the RAPTOR web UI and API. A developer should look at `raptor/server/cli.py` first to understand how the application initializes, configures logging and environment settings, and boots via `uvicorn.run()`. The `serve()` function orchestrates this startup process, relying on `raptor.server.config.ServerSettings` and `raptor.server.app`. 

Concurrently, `raptor/server/schemas.py` defines the domain-specific data contracts consumed and produced by the application. It uses Pydantic `BaseModel` classes—categorized across indexes, trees, queries, evaluations, and code analysis—to establish the OpenAPI schema for frontend communication without performing any I/O or side effects.

Concept: configuration management
Concept: configuration management

These files work together to provide declarative, Pydantic-based configuration management across the codebase. `raptor/config.py` acts as the primary system config via `RaptorConfig`, handling general index building and querying settings. `raptor/code/config.py` handles domain-specific code indexing and retrieval settings through the root class `CodeConfig`. Both root classes support YAML loading, exporting, and SHA-256 state hashing via `from_yaml()`, `to_yaml()`, and `fingerprint()`. Separately, `raptor/server/config.py` defines API operational settings, paths, and server limits using the `ServerSettings` model. 

A developer should look first at `raptor/config.py` for core indexing parameters, `raptor/code/config.py` for code-specific settings, and `raptor/server/config.py` for API server parameters.

Concept: code retrieval and evaluation framework

Concept: Web UI Server API

These files implement the FastAPI-based web UI server for RAPTOR.

Concept: Command-line interface and tool integration
